expectations.evidence: Document names HEMLIG and KVALIFICERAT HEMLIG (lines 5, 696) but never mentions BEGRÄNSAT HEMLIG. Only two of the three levels are named.
Säkerhetsskyddslagen (2018:585) is referenced extensively as the governing framework (section 2.1, line 62+), including subordinate regulations and specific chapter references in Appendix C.
FMV and MUST are named repeatedly as the accreditation authorities (lines 8, 35, 78-88, section 14 accreditation roadmap). Document is framed as draft for FMV/MUST accreditation review.

Säpo is acknowledged for administering security clearances (line 69: 'Sapo-administered security clearance'), referenced in personnel model (line 41: 'Sapo security clearances'), and the security officer interfaces with Säpo (line 913).

TEMPEST/EMSEC addressed in detail: SDIP-27 Level A or B, Faraday cage, filtered power lines, fiber-only connections (lines 157-161), EMSEC zone inspected by MUST, annual TEMPEST assessment in risk register.

Document explicitly designs around 12 cleared engineers out of 40 total (lines 41, 55, 514-541), with detailed role breakdown (4 SRE, 2 security, 4 dev, 2 data) and sustainability planning for the small team.

Line 40: 'All data, processing, metadata, backups, and key material remain within Swedish territory at all times, in facilities controlled by Swedish-cleared personnel.' Appendix C reiterates: 'All data in Sweden, air-gapped, no foreign cloud.'

Air gap is treated as physical separation: 'zero IP-routable connections' (line 232), no wireless interfaces, USB ports epoxy-filled, only physical media transfer crosses the boundary (section 5.1, 9.2).

Line 82: 'Swedish-approved crypto only for HEMLIG'. Line 694-696: MUST specifies approved algorithms/products; for KVALIFICERAT HEMLIG, Swedish national crypto (Tutus/Advenica) would be required. Distinguishes from mere FIPS compliance.

Hardware data diode (Advenica SecuriCDS) for one-way export (line 219, 238), content filtering/sanitization before diode (line 856), media transfer procedures with two-person integrity (section 9.2). Addresses CDS approval for NATO/EU sharing (line 100).

Document uses predominantly open-source tools (Appendix A lists Apache 2.0/MIT/GPL licenses) and mentions 'no vendor lock-in' for Ceph, but never explicitly states a FLOSS preference policy or the caveat that certified/approved products take precedence where required.

While the Swedish framework is primary, the document makes significant US-centric references: RKE2 selected partly for 'DISA STIG compliance' (line 326), 'CIS Kubernetes Benchmark' (line 325), 'FIPS 140-2/140-3 compliant crypto modules' (line 323), and HSMs specified as 'FIPS 140-3 Level 3' (line 220). These US standards are presented as design drivers rather than secondary references.
